test_title: PYST 40: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 01 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A primary goal of LPG reforms was macroeconomic stabilisation. Which indicator improved significantly post-1991 reforms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Foreign Exchange Reserves**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **LPG reforms** (Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation) were introduced in India in **1991** to address the economic crisis of the time.
 
• One of the key objectives of the reforms was **macroeconomic stabilisation**, which aimed to strengthen India's economy through structural adjustments.
 
• Post-1991 reforms, India's **foreign exchange reserves** improved significantly. The reserves increased from a precarious level of less than **$1 billion** in 1991 to robust levels in subsequent years.
 
• This improvement was driven by increased **foreign investment**, higher **exports**, and a more liberalised trade policy.
 
• Strengthened foreign exchange reserves provided India with greater economic stability and reduced its vulnerability to external economic shocks.
 
• The reforms also facilitated a shift towards a more open and competitive economy, encouraging growth in industries and enhancing India's **global trade position**.
 
• The improvement in foreign exchange reserves was critical in ensuring that the country could manage its imports and meet its international financial obligations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Revenue Deficit**__

 __
 
• Revenue deficit refers to the shortfall between the government's revenue receipts and its revenue expenditure.
 
• While the LPG reforms aimed to improve fiscal management, addressing revenue deficit remained a gradual process.
 
• Revenue deficit reduction required structural reforms in taxation and government expenditure.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Deficit**__
 __
 
• Fiscal deficit is the difference between total revenue and total expenditure of the government, excluding borrowings.
 
• Although fiscal deficit was targeted under the LPG reforms, it did not improve significantly immediately after the reforms.
 
• It required sustained efforts in fiscal discipline and reduction of subsidies over time.
 
 
 
• **Rural Unemployment**__
 
 
• Rural unemployment refers to the lack of job opportunities in rural areas.
 
• Though the LPG reforms contributed to overall economic growth, addressing rural unemployment required focused initiatives like **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** implemented later.
